children: Apple briefly crossed the historic valuation during Tuesday’s session. A record close now rests on its measured AI strategy, new enterprise Macs and an unusually expensive foldable iPhone.
Five trillion, almost
Apple shares
gained 0.2% Tuesday to close at $339.75, their highest finish since July 28. That valued the company at $4.96 trillion,
. Based on the current share count, a closing price above $342.602 would carry Apple through the $5 trillion threshold.
The stock reached $345.34 intraday, briefly pushing its market value above $5 trillion before surrendering part of the advance.
Apple also crossed that line during trading on July 28 and 29, but it has never wrapped up a regular session above it.

Nvidia is the only other company to have traded above $5 trillion, reaching the milestone in October 2025. Apple’s approach is built differently: investors are rewarding a consumer-hardware and services business that has avoided matching its rivals’ enormous AI infrastructure budgets.
Apple makes the quieter AI bet
Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet and Meta are investing heavily in data centers, chips and power capacity, placing pressure on near-term free cash flow.
Apple has emphasized custom silicon, on-device processing and selective cloud infrastructure — an approach that looks increasingly defensive when investors become nervous about AI spending.

Its new high-end Mac Mini and Mac Studio models extend that strategy into the enterprise market. Apple argues that companies can run AI workloads locally without repeatedly paying cloud providers for tokens, with configurations costing nearly $20,000 aimed at developers and corporate buyers.
Apple demonstrated four Mac Studios running a trillion-parameter model from one wall outlet, highlighting the efficiency of its unified-memory architecture.
The challenge is distribution: Macs hold roughly 4.6% of the enterprise desktop market against more than 91% for Windows, while Nvidia remains firmly entrenched in data-center AI.
Ternus starts with Apple’s biggest iPhone change
John Ternus became CEO at the beginning of September, replacing Tim Cook, and immediately inherited a major product cycle.
The $1,999 iPhone Duo introduces
and the largest physical redesign since the original iPhone arrived.

The Duo combines a 7.6-inch inner display with a 5.4-inch outer screen, allowing two applications to run side by side. Preorders begin October 16 ahead of the October 23 release, giving traders an early measure of whether consumers will accept Apple’s most expensive phone yet.

, particularly after higher memory costs also forced Apple to raise prices on its Pro models.

However, even moderate Duo sales could lift the average selling price and margins. For the stock, $342.60 is the immediate milestone; after that, product demand must justify the five-trillion-dollar valuation.
